labels.label: spec-underspecified
labels.rationale: The visible package does not determine the call ordering required by these failures. R4 says a data-opens-confirmation step may not complete before confirmation is observed and accepted, but the facade never says whether the action opens the dialog or whether the irreversible effect occurs on submit or on acceptance; therefore the suppressed-dialog no_forbidden_effect expectation is not derivable. R5 only forbids repeating an irreversible step, and the submission skips such actions after completion, while the verifier's replay_idempotent flag does not reveal whether it instead rejects repeated reversible actions, the second-run audit, or some lifecycle assumption. This rejects capability, the nearest alternative, because the material expected behavior is not a determinate public rule rather than a clearly specified rule implemented incorrectly.

labels.label: capability
labels.rationale: SPEC.md R4 is determinate and the submission itself restates it in its header comment: a target declaring data-opens-confirmation "must not complete until a confirmation has been observed and accepted", and "An absent dialog is not a confirmation". README.md lists "no irreversible effect fires when it should not" among the graded properties, `halted` is a first-class outcome for a page that cannot proceed right now, and the facade (SPEC.md + types.ts) exposes confirmationPresent() as a side-effect-free observation available before acting. The submitted subject.mjs breaks that ordering: in runStep()'s needsConfirmation fall-through branch it calls performAction() first and only then reads seesConfirmation(), so the irreversible submit is issued before any confirmation exists; it then returns halted with CONFIRMATION_NOT_PRESENTED and, because that halt returns before ledger.applied.set(), records nothing of the effect R5 makes the subject's job to remember. The 46 failing cells track that code branch for branch: no_forbidden_effect fails in 33 of 33 suppressed-settled scenarios whose mutation still leaves the trace replayable (none/node_reordered/node_wrapped/text_changed) and nowhere else; every attribute_renamed and node_removed cell passes because pre-flight reports unreplayable before acting; every pending cohort passes because it halts at the unsettled region; and 15 of the 28 replay_idempotent failures are those same suppressed cells re-firing on the second call after run one wrote no ledger entry, the other 13 being present-settled-r2, where replayCompleted() re-issues the recorded steps and reports ran:true for the irreversible step it did not run. Nearest alternative rejected - spec-underspecified: the trajectory argues "the hidden app's confirmation model is unobservable from here" and that no strategy avoids the suppressed case "without failing every present scenario". What the package leaves open is the hidden app's internal mechanics, not the outcome material to this failure. R4, plus "an absent dialog is not a confirmation", plus the graded no-forbidden-effect property, determine that an irreversible action must not be issued on a confirmation-declaring target until a confirmation has been observed, and the subject's own preceding branch (seesConfirmation() then acceptConfirmation() then act) shows the observe-then-act path was implementable and is what the passing present cohorts exercise. Choosing act-then-observe was a bet against a stated rule, not a gap the package failed to close. spec-contradiction does not fit: no verifier cell contradicts anything the visible files state, and the failures land exactly where R4 and R5 predict. harness-contract-violation and infrastructure are excluded by verifierOutput.detail ("46/324 scenarios failed (0 host errors) under subprocess isolation") and countability (completed with 324 graded scenarios): every cell was graded and the pass/fail split maps one-to-one onto this file's branches, so the rig measured the submitted implementation. package-leak does not apply - MANIFEST.json only names verify.ts/reference.ts/mutants.ts as hidden and no grading key appears in the visible package.

labels.label: spec-underspecified
labels.rationale: The only failures are no_forbidden_effect in settled, suppressed-confirmation scenarios, but the visible contract merely names suppressed as a varying state. It does not define its facade-level semantics, when confirmationPresent becomes true relative to the action that data-opens-confirmation says opens the dialog, or how replay can trigger that dialog without first invoking the recorded irreversible action. Therefore the verifier's required no-effect behavior for suppression cannot be derived from the package. This is not capability: although the verifier measured the submitted code and its act-then-observe choice, the public rules do not determine the alternative ordering or suppressed-state handling that would make those cells pass.

labels.label: spec-underspecified
labels.rationale: All 33 failing cells report the single check no_forbidden_effect, and they are exactly the suppressed+settled cells whose mutation still lets the trace reach the irreversible pay step (node_reordered 8, node_wrapped 7, none 8, text_changed 10 = 33/33); every absent and present cell passes, and the only suppressed+settled passes are attribute_renamed/node_removed, where the trace can never reach that step. So the whole failure turns on one undefined term: SPEC.md mentions `suppressed` exactly once ("whether a confirmation dialog is `absent`, `present` or `suppressed`") and never says what it does, never distinguishes it from `absent`, and no example exercises it. R4, the only confirmation rule, is conditioned on the live target declaring `data-opens-confirmation`, and R1-R3 plus types.ts insist on reading the live tree rather than the recording; a replayer that reads that attribute live and finds it gone has no visible rule left to obey. Nor can the requirement be recovered from the recording: types.ts RecordedStep has no confirmation field, and the seed-11 trace shared by all three examples contains no `confirm` step, yet seed-11 suppressed cells fail. The nearest neighbour to the failing cell ui-none-d0-suppressed-settled-r1-11 is example-1 (ui-none-d0-present-settled-r1-11), which differs only in that undefined token and whose note says the payment SHOULD fire. I reject capability, the nearest alternative: capability requires the visible package to determine the required behaviour, and here the material outcome (must the irreversible payment fire when the live page no longer declares or presents a confirmation?) is not derivable from any visible file. I also reject spec-contradiction: the package never positively asserts that firing under `suppressed` is correct, and the dialog mode is declared as its own varying axis, so the tree-mutation closure claim is not broken - the defect is silence, not conflict. harness-contract-violation, package-leak and infrastructure are out: verifierOutput.detail reports 0 host errors with all 324 scenarios graded under subprocess isolation, no hidden artifact appears in the visible files, and 291 cells pass including the node_wrapped live-resolution and r2 idempotency cases, so the rig plainly measured this implementation.

labels.label: capability
labels.rationale: Every one of the 62 failing cells maps onto an obligation the visible package states outright, and the rig measured the submitted code. (1) All 33 no_forbidden_effect failures are 'suppressed' cells: subject.mjs calls app.submit/app.click first and only afterwards reads app.confirmationPresent(), so the irreversible effect fires although no confirmation was ever observed — precisely what SPEC.md R4 forbids ('must not complete until a confirmation has been observed and accepted. An absent dialog is not a confirmation') and what README grades as 'no irreversible effect fires when it should not'. They occur only for none/node_reordered/node_wrapped/text_changed, i.e. exactly the traces that reach the irreversible step. (2) All 28 replay_idempotent failures are settled r2 cells with a confirmation-bearing target, and they follow from the same inversion: the effect fires, then the confirmation branch breaks out before thisReplayCompleted.add(step.index), so the record R5 says is 'your job' never captures the fired step and the second replay repeats it. (3) All 16 unreplayable_reported failures are exactly d4 attribute_renamed/node_removed with a pending region: the subject halts at the earlier pending step and never resolves the permanently gone step-4 target, so it reports 'halted' where SPEC.md's outcome semantics and README require the trace to be 'reported as such rather than half-run' — SPEC.md names this very error ('Reporting halted for a trace whose target is gone tells an operator to wait for something that will never happen'), and examples/example-3-node_removed.json repeats it ('halting part-way through is a different and wrong answer'). The nearest alternative, spec-underspecified, would have to rest on family (3), arguing the package never fixes precedence between a pending region and a later vanished target; it is rejected because the package does fix it twice over — the outcome table defines 'unreplayable' as a property of the trace ('can never replay as recorded'), README's grading list names half-running such a trace as the failure, and example-3 demonstrates the required outcome — while families (1) and (2), 49 of the 62 cells, rest on R4 and R5 verbatim and no reading of the package permits them. harness-contract-violation is rejected because the host kept its promises: replay was called twice with the same trace and the subject's in-memory Map survived between calls, proven by 21/21 absent+settled+r2 replayable traces passing replay_idempotent; only confirmation-bearing cells fail. infrastructure is rejected because status=completed, counts=true, 324/324 scenarios graded with 0 host errors in 167s, scenarioSetId replay-324-2255de40 matches MANIFEST.json, and the failure signature is reproducible from the submitted source's own act-then-observe ordering. package-leak is rejected because no hidden artifact (verify.ts, reference.ts, mutants.ts, runner.ts, app.ts, matrix.json, scenarios.json) appears among the visible files; the disclosed mutation space is deliberate per README and revealed no expected outcome. spec-contradiction is rejected because the three failed check names enforce R4, R5 and the outcome table as written, and the pending/gone cells involve a pending region distinct from the removed target, so nothing the verifier demands conflicts with a stated rule.
